faqs.q: What is the minimum wage for a 20 year old in Australia?
faqs.a: The minimum wage for a 20-year-old depends on the applicable award or enterprise agreement. The national minimum wage for adults is $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026, but junior rates are typically a percentage of the adult rate. Check your award on the Fair Work Ombudsman website for the exact figure.

faqs.q: How do I convert hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week (usually 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.88 annually. This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime or penalty rates.

faqs.q: Does super guarantee apply to minimum wage?
faqs.a: Yes, super guarantee of 12% is paid on top of ordinary earnings, including minimum wage, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This means your total remuneration includes the super amount, which is separate from your hourly rate.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Minimum Wage for a 20 Year Old Australia

If you are 20 years old and working in Australia, you may be wondering how your hourly rate compares to an annual salary. The keyword 'minimum wage for a 20 year old Australia is a common search term, and this guide will help you convert your hourly rate to annual pay, fortnightly pay, and super. We use the 38-hour week and 52-week year as standard. 

### The National Minimum Wage vs. Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for adults, and $1004.9 per week for 38 hours. However, for 20-year-old, the minimum wage is not necessarily the adult rate. Under many awards, junior employees receive a percentage of the adult rate. For example, a 20-year-old might get 85% of the adult rate, but this varies by industry. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides specific junior rates in each award. Always check your award or agreement for the correct minimum wage for a 20 year old Australia.

### How to Convert Hourly to Annual Gross Pay

The formula is simple: hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the annual gross pay is hourly × 1,976 (38 × 52). For example, if the minimum wage for a 20 year old Australia under your award is $22.47 per hour (hypothetical), then annual gross = $22.47 × 38 × 52 = $44,424.72. This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. Use [the timesheet](/) to quickly compute your own figures.

### Fortnightly Pay

If you are paid fortnightly, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Weekly pay is hourly rate × hours per week. For 38 hours, weekly = hourly × 38. Fortnightly = weekly × 2. For the example above, weekly = $22.47 × 38 = $853.86, fortnightly = $1,707.72.

### Casual Loading and Super

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. The base rate is the minimum wage for a 20 year old Australia (or award rate). Do not include casual loading in the base rate you enter in [the timesheet](/) – the checkbox adds it automatically. For casuals, the loaded rate is base × 1.25. Super guarantee of 12% is paid on top of ordinary earnings, including the base rate and any casual loading. Super does not come out of your pocket; it is additional. The maximum contribution base for super is $270,830 per year.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

For 2026–27, resident tax rates: nil up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% from $45,001 to $135,000; 37% from $135,001 to $190,000; 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy is generally 2%. The tax-free threshold is included. For a full-time worker on the minimum wage for a 20 year old Australia, tax will be low. Use [pay guides](/blog) for more details on tax estimates.

### Important Disclaimer

This annual pay estimate is based on hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
